title: INITIAL CLINICAL TRIAL TO EVALUATE THE SAFETY AND POTENTIAL BENEFIT OF BONE MARROW–DERIVED STEM CELLS IN CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS WITH CEREBRAL ADRENOLEUKODYSTROPHY
official: OPEN-LABEL, PHASE I CLINICAL TRIAL TO EVALUATE THE SAFETY AND PRELIMINARY CLINICAL RESPONSE TO THE USE OF ALLOGENEIC BONE MARROW MESENCHYMAL STEM CELLS IN CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS WITH X-LINKED ADRENOLEUKODYSTROPHY CEREBRAL FORM.
summary: Main objective: To assess the safety of allogeneic bone marrow mesenchymal cell infusion in children with X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy, administered via the intrathecal route in selected cases.

interventions.name: Bone marrow-derived Mesenchymal Stromal Cells  cryopreserved at passage P2, thawed, washed and syringe-conditioned in  0.9% NaCl - 0.5% human serum albumin injection solution at a dose of 5.10^6  Mesenchymal Stromal Cells

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. - Male patients under 16 years of age with a diagnosis confirmed by genetic study and determination of long-chain fatty acids in blood yorin, of X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy who cannot be included in treatment with haematopoietic progenitor transplantation (due to not having a compatible donor or having a Loes and NFS greater than that stipulated in the centre) or gene therapy (Skysona® (only approved in the USA)). - Patients with acceptable residual capacities: an NFS score of ≤ 6/25 is established. - Patients with contrast uptake (GIS) ≥ 1 in CMR.  - Possibility of performing CMR and neuropsychological assessments. - Acceptance of informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
1. - Male patients with X-ALD who are candidates for treatment with haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (by compatible donor and with Loes and NFS values that do not contraindicate) or gene therapy (Skysona ® -only approved in the EEUU-).  - Stopped forms of X-ALD regardless of score (radiological stability for more than 12 months) and presymptomatic patients (familial diagnosis).  - Concomitant diseases such as: o Active CNS or systemic infections. o Active tumour  - Haematological alteration contraindicating lumbar puncture - Refusal of the patient or family members to follow up adequately
